rows: All strains have been genotyped for 2,955 genetic markers, 1,969 of which exhibited unique segregation patterns among the 95 segregant strains.
We looked for linkage between inheritance of these 1,969 markers and the 354 transcript and protein levels using t tests and determined FDR cutoffs for each gene on the basis of 100 permutations.
At a 5% FDR, we mapped 49 and 97 loci that control the level of a total of 125 and 200 proteins and transcripts, respectively.
At a 1% FDR, we mapped 30 and 74 loci that control levels of 89 and 170 proteins and transcripts, respectively ( Table S4 ).
the total number of linkages at a 5% FDR was 179 for proteins and 342 for transcripts, and at a 1% FDR these numbers were 115 and 253, respectively.
at 1% FDR, we map regulators of 170 transcripts, 22 of which act in cis. In contrast, at this FDR we map regulators of 89 proteins, only three of which act in cis
We found that proteins and transcripts were well correlated for only 27% of genes (94/354 at 5% significance; Table S3 )
The dashed lines at 0.24 and 0.31 indicate the average cutoffs for significance at p <0.05 and p <0.01, respectively
averages for proteins and transcripts were 0.70 and 0.71, respectively, and medians for proteins and transcripts were 0.71 and 0.74, respectively
The levels of protein ACS2 are higher in segregants that inherited SNP 12_662,627 from the RM (vineyard) compared to segregants that inherited this SNP from the BY (laboratory) parent.
both proteins and transcripts show hot spots of regulation (single loci that control multiple genes), (2) these hot spots are largely but not completely overlapping
Raw data for both protein [14] and transcript [17] , [19] , [21] quantitation came from previously published work.
The mapping algorithm was based on t tests with permutation testing to determine false discovery rates. Complete code is available from E.J.F. upon request.
